about: Seven laws on the inheritance of women of several classes, most of them dedicated to a god, and on the dowry of a šugītum. A woman of the NIN.AN, SAL or zikrum class whose father gave her a dowry and wrote a tablet for her, but did not write that she may give her estate to whomever she pleases, holds her field and orchard as long as she lives, and her brothers have the right to them after her; if her brothers fail to give her her rations of grain, oil and wool, she may give the land to a tenant who is pleasing to her, who must keep supporting her (§178). If the tablet does allow her to give her estate to whomever it pleases her, her brothers have no claim against her (§179). A woman of the kallātum or zikrum class whose father gave her no dowry takes a share in her father’s house like one heir, for her lifetime (§180); a qadištum or a NU.PAR dedicated to a god without a dowry takes one third of an heir’s share, for her lifetime (§181); and a “wife of Marduk” of Babylon whose father gave her neither a dowry nor a sealed tablet takes one third of an heir’s share with her brothers, performs no fief-duty, and may give her estate to whomever it pleases her (§182). The last two laws concern the šugītum: if her father gave her a dowry, a husband and a sealed tablet she has no further share in his house (§183), but if he gave her neither dowry nor husband, her brothers must give her a dowry in proportion to the means of the house and give her to a husband (§184). The classes of woman are named by Sumerian sign-groups (NIN.AN, SAL, NU.GIG, NU.PAR, SAL.É.GI₄.A) and by words whose exact meaning is still argued; the notes mark each reading as certain or uncertain.

sentences.i: If a priestess (?), a SAL-woman (?), or a woman of the zikrum class, to whom her father has given a dowry,
sentences.n: The first of seven laws on what women of certain priestly classes inherit, and a law with a long “if”, so read it clause by clause; this unit only names the woman. šumma is “if” as always, but the subject is a woman. NIN.AN is a Sumerogram of two signs, read ugbabtum “priestess” as at §127: UNCERTAIN (Harper gives no reading and later editions read the signs differently). The sign after it is Harper’s ŠAL(?), the woman-sign SAL with his own question mark; I give it as SAL and no more, since a lone SAL is read as a class of priestess by some later editions (compare §40), UNCERTAIN. On the plate NIN is drawn as two parts, a six-sided sign and a small box, then AN, and the SAL (six-sided sign with a long tail) stands on a lower tier at the right end of the line (at XXXI 20 it stands on the line itself). ù lū zinništum zikrum is “or else a woman, a zikrum”: ù “and, or”, lū “or indeed”, SAL read zinništum “woman” (as at §141–152), and zi-ik-ru-um, zikrum, the name of a class of woman; it is not the zikrum “name” of the prologue, and what the class was I cannot say, UNCERTAIN (the SAL before zi-ik-ru-um may instead be a woman-sign belonging to the class name, like the SAL before kallātim and qadištam below; I follow Harper’s zinništum zikrum). ša abūša šeriqtam išruqušim is “whom her father has given a dowry”: ša opens a relative clause that runs through the next unit (watch for this pattern; it comes back at every law); abūša is “her father”, šeriqtam “a dowry” (§138), and išruqušim is išruq, “he gave (as a gift)”, from šarāqum, with the subjunctive -u and -šim “to her” (short u before -šim, the house rule); the -šim looks back to the woman, so the clause reads “whom … he gave her a dowry”. Harper prints iš-ru-qu-ši-im; the sign is KU, read qu₂.

sentences.n: What the tablet left out: two things, both with lā “not”. warkassa ēma eliša ṭābu nadānam is “her estate, wherever it is pleasing to her, to give”: warkassa is warkatum “estate” + -ša “her” (t+š written ss, the spelling wa-ar-ka-za of §141–152), ēma “wherever”, eliša ṭābu “it is pleasing to her” (eli “upon”, ṭâbum “to be good”; the verb is in the subjunctive -u after ēma), and nadānam the infinitive “to give”; I read the clause as “to give her estate to whomever she pleases” (house rendering). lā išṭuršimma is “he has not written for her, and”: išṭur + -šim “to her” + -ma; lā with the preterite is “has not”. mala libbiša is “as much as her heart (wants)”. lā ušamziši is “he has not let her have”: a Š-stem preterite (the spelling u-ša-am-zi-ši) with -ši “her”; the verb behind it is UNCERTAIN, and the sense “let her have her fill” is taken from the context.

sentences.i: she shall give her field and her orchard to a tenant who is pleasing to her, and her tenant shall keep supporting her.
sentences.n: The ruling: she lets the land out herself. eqlša u kirâša as above, now objects of inaddinma “she shall give, and”. ana irrišim ša eliša ṭābu is “to a tenant who is pleasing to her”: irrišum “tenant”, then the ša-clause with eliša ṭābu as at §178. irrissa is “her tenant”: irrišum + -ša, the š+š spelled with ZA (ir-ri-za; the same spelling as irrissu at §42–51). ittanaššiši is “he shall keep supporting her”: the iterative present (Gtn: it-ta-na-… “again and again”) of našûm “to carry, bear” + -ši “her”, spelled it-ta-na-aš-ši-ši, with the single-wedge sign AŠ read aš; “supporting” is my sense for what a tenant owes her, UNCERTAIN.

sentences.i: She shall have the use of the field, the orchard and whatever her father gave her as long as she lives; she shall not give (them) for silver,
sentences.n: What she may and may not do with the land. eqlam kirâm u mimma ša abūša iddinušim is “the field, the orchard and whatever her father gave her”: the two accusative objects (A.ŠÀ; {giš}KIRI₆), mimma “whatever”, and ša abūša iddinušim “which her father gave her” (the ša-clause with -šim, as at the start of §178). adi balṭat ikkal is “as long as she is alive she shall eat (have the use of it)”: adi “as long as”, balṭat “she is alive” (stative of balāṭum), ikkal the present of akālum “to eat”, here spelled ì-kal (the sign NI read ì, then KAL); “eat” for “have the use of” is as at §170–177 and UNCERTAIN. ana kaspim ul inaddin is “for silver she shall not give”: kaspim is the Sumerogram KÙ.BABBAR with no ending written.

sentences.i: nor shall she pay another (with them) (?); her heirship belongs to her brothers alone.
sentences.n: šaniam ul uppal is “another she shall not pay (?)”: šaniam “another” (accusative; apālum “to pay” takes the person paid as its object, as in tamkāram ippalū at §141–152) and uppal, a present I take to be from apālum (u-up-pa-al, the vowel pattern is unusual); “with them” is supplied from the context, and the whole clause is UNCERTAIN. ablūssa ša aḫḫīšama is “her heirship belongs to her brothers alone”: ablūssa is ablūtum “the status of an heir” + -ša (t+š written ss, as in warkassa; ab-lu-za), and ša aḫḫīšama is “that of her brothers only” (aḫḫīša is aḫḫū in the genitive, -ma “only”). When she dies, the land passes to her brothers.

and

not (in subordinate and nominal contexts) · before a noun in the genitive, “without”: lā kanīkim “without a sealed receipt”; in a šumma-clause, “not”: lā ītamar “he did not see”

to her, for her (dative suffix -šim, on a verb; the feminine counterpart of -šum): inaddiššim “he shall give her”, utarrūšim “they shall return to her”, inaddinūšimma “they shall give her, and”, ušallamšimma “he shall make (it) whole for her, and”; not the accusative -ši “her” of ukabbilšima and ubbiršima

sentences.i: If a father has not given a dowry to his daughter, a kallatum (?) or a zikrum-woman,
sentences.n: A new case: the father gave no dowry at all. ana mārtišu is “to his daughter”: DUMU.SAL (two signs) + šu; Harper writes mârti-šu. kallātim is {šal}É.GI₄.A, the woman-sign SAL (Harper’s raised šal, silent here) and the three signs É.GI₄.A, which at §153–169 meant “bride, daughter-in-law”; here it seems to name a class of woman dedicated to a god, which I cannot define: UNCERTAIN. ù lū zinništim zikrum is “or else a woman, a zikrum” as at §178; Harper’s genitive zinništi is zinništim here, since it stands beside mārtišu kallātim in apposition (“his daughter, a kallatum or a zikrum-woman”). šeriqtam lā išruqšim is “a dowry he has not given her”: išruqšim is išruq + -šim, with no -u because this is a plain verb, no ša-clause; on the plate the RU is not written at all (IŠ, then UG, ŠI, IM; compare XXXI 65, where the curl-shaped RU stands between IŠ and UG), so the scribe left it out and Harper restores it in brackets; the glyph is kept, marked [ru], and the form rests on the same word at §181, iš-ru-uq-ši-im.

sentences.i: After the father has gone to his fate, she shall take a share from the property of her father’s house like one heir, and

sentences.i: If a father has not given a dowry to his daughter, a wife of Marduk of Babylon, and has not written a sealed tablet for her,
sentences.n: The next class is named after her god. aššat Marduk is “the wife of Marduk”: SAL stands bare and is read aššat (the construct, “wife of”, as at §127–140, where aššatum is written out), and {d}AMAR.UTU is Marduk (the AN sign silent, AMAR.UTU “calf of the sun”, as in the prologue). ša Bābilim is “of Babylon”: the Sumerogram KÁ.DINGIR.RA{ki}, “gate of the god”, read Bābilim (as in the litany), with the KI sign printed full size on the plate. The “wife of Marduk” is a title of a priestess of the god; what more she was I cannot say, UNCERTAIN. šeriqtam lā išruqšim is “a dowry he has not given her”; kunukkam lā išṭuršim is “a sealed tablet he has not written for her”, with no -ma at the end of this protasis.

sentences.i: After the father has gone to his fate, she shall take one third of her heir’s share from the property of her father’s house together with her brothers, and she shall not perform the fief-duty;
sentences.n: She takes a third, as at §181, with her brothers; no “for life” limit is repeated, and she owes no fief-duty. itti aḫḫīša izzazma is “with her brothers she shall stand (take her place), and”. ilkam ul illak is “she shall not perform the fief-duty”: ilkam is ilkum written il-kam (the signs IL and KAM, as the “fief-duty” of §26–41), with ul … illak “she shall not go”; alākum “to go” with ilkum is “to carry out the service”. The text gives no reason, and I do not supply one.

sentences.i: If a father has given a dowry to his daughter, a šugītum, and has given her to a husband, and has written a sealed tablet for her,
sentences.n: The šugītum (a class of woman, UNCERTAIN, as at §137) is the woman first met there (there with a raised SAL; Harper prints šu-ge-tim here without it, and the plate shows only the three signs ŠU, GI₄, TIM). ana mārtišu šugītim is “to his daughter, a šugītum”, in apposition. šeriqtam išruqšim is “a dowry he has given her”, with no lā this time; ana mutim iddišši is “to a husband he has given her”: mutim is “husband” (short u, as at §127–140) and iddišši is iddin + -ši “her”, the n written as š (id-di-iš-ši). kunukkam išṭuršim is “a sealed tablet he has written for her” (ku-nu-uk-kam, the sign UG read uk). This is a protasis; the ruling is the next unit.

sentences.i: her brothers shall give her a dowry in proportion to the means of her father’s house, and shall give her to a husband.
sentences.n: The ruling: the brothers must provide for her. aḫḫūša kīma emūq bīt abim is “her brothers, in proportion to the strength of her father’s house” (emūq “strength”, as at §178; “means” is my English for it): kīma + emūq + bīt abim, with É and a-ba. šeriqtam išarraqūšima is “they shall give her a dowry, and”: išarraqū is the present plural of šarāqum (the same verb as išruq above, with its middle r doubled), then -ši “her” and -ma, spelled i-šar-ra-qu₂-ši-ma. ana mutim inaddinūši is “to a husband they shall give her”: inaddinū the present plural of nadānum + -ši.

glossary.-šu: his / him · -šum “to him, for him” (dative): išakkanūšum, innadnušum · after a dental the suffix is assimilated and spelled with z: …ssu (ṣibat-zu, ṣibassu “its interest”, written after a broken sign); with a noun: ṣibtišu “its interest”, qātīšu “his hand”, damqaršu “his merchant”; tu-šu, te-šu in broken forms · with the same assimilation after a t: aššassu (aš-ša-zu) “his wife”, from aššat + -šu, t + š said ss · on a verb, the object “him”, or “to him” in the dative (Harper writes -šu for -šum): imaggarūšu (i-ma-ag-ga-ru-šu) “they shall agree to him”; on a noun after a preposition: elišu “upon him” · on a Š-stem, “him”: ušaḫḫazūšu “they shall have him take”, ušeṣṣûšu “they shall make him go out” · uktarriṣṣu (ug-dar-ri-zu) “he has slandered him” (ṣ + š said ṣṣ, spelled with ZU) · ikassûšuma “they shall bind him, and” · on nouns: emišu “his father-in-law’s”, ibiršu “his friend”, rabītišu “his senior one”, warkassu “his case”, zittišu “his share”, īnšu “his eye”
glossary.NU.PAR: NU.PAR (the signs NU and PAR, the BAR sign) — a second class of woman, named beside the qadištum (§181); given as the signs only, with no reading and no translation, UNCERTAIN · Sumerogram, untranslated
glossary.SAL-sign: SAL — the woman-sign standing alone after NIN.AN in §178–179 (Harper’s ŠAL(?)); given as the sign and no more, since a lone SAL is read by some later editions as a class of priestess, UNCERTAIN; not read as a word here (compare zinništum and aššat, where SAL is read) · Sumerogram, untranslated
glossary.SIG.BA: SIG.BA (SIG + BA) — “wool ration” (SIG wool, BA allowance), one of the three rations of §178–179 (Harper writes ŠIG.BA); the Akkadian word behind it is not read, UNCERTAIN · Sumerogram, Akkadian word not read
glossary.ablūtum: sonship, the status of a son (Harper’s word, from ablum “son”): ina ablūtim (ab-lu-tim) “from sonship”; nasāḫim ina ablūtim “to cast out of sonship” · ablūssa (ab-lu-za), ablūtiša (ab-lu-ti-ša) “her heirship”, the status or share of an heir (not “sonship” here, the heir being a daughter): ablūssa ša aḫḫīšama “her heirship belongs to her brothers alone”; šalšat ablūtiša “a third of her heirship”
glossary.abum: father: ilik abišu “his father’s fief-duty” · abī (a-bi) construct “father of”: abī mārtim “the father of the daughter” · abim written a-ba in bīt abim (Harper’s spelling, UNCERTAIN)
glossary.adi: up to, times: adi 12-šu “twelvefold” · as a conjunction, “as long as”, with the subjunctive: adi kirâm ṣabtu “as long as he holds the orchard” · adu 3-šu, adu 6-šu “three times, six times (as much)” — the multiplier, spelled a-du (Harper’s variant of adi; the plate has the sign DU) · adi šinīšu “up to his second time” = a second time (as adi 10-šu “tenfold”)
glossary.akālum: to eat; infinitive akālum “eating, food”: akālim “of eating”, in ša akālim ibašši “there is food” (literally “something of eating”) · with a possession as object or alone, “to have the use of” (a house, an estate), literally “to eat it”: ikkal (i-ik-ka-al, present) in adi balṭat ikkal “as long as she lives she shall eat (have the use of it)”; the sense “have the use of” is UNCERTAIN · ikkal also written ì-kal (the sign NI read ì, then KAL): adi balṭat ikkal “as long as she lives she shall have the use of it”
glossary.alākum: to go: illak “he shall go” · illiku “(where) he went” (preterite, subjunctive -u, after a restored ašar), in the agent law · alākišu (a-la-ki-šu) “his going” (infinitive with -šu): ina alākišu “in his going” · Gt present ittallak (it-ta-al-la-ak) “she shall go away” (the Gt gives the sense of going off; the Gtn would be ittanallak) · ittalak “she has gone” (perfect): ana šīmtim ittalak “she has gone to her fate” · ittalku (it-ta-al-ku) with the subjunctive -u: warka abum ana šīmtim ittalku “after the father has gone to his fate”
glossary.ana: to, for · with an infinitive, “to, for” (ana kirîm zaqāpim “to plant as an orchard”); “as” (ana kirîm), “into” (ana libbi), “at the rate of” (ana itêšu)
glossary.aplum: heir, son as heir (Harper aplu; spelled ab-lim, the sign read ab or ap): aplim “of an heir”, in kīma aplim ištēn “like one heir” · also written with the signs DUMU.UŠ (Harper TUR.UŠ, ablu), unspelled: aplum “the heir”, the son who inherits; the Sumerian writing can also mean “eldest son”, the choice rests on the clause (UNCERTAIN)
glossary.apālum: to answer; to satisfy, pay (a creditor): ippalma (present, with -ma) “he shall pay, and” · uppal (u-up-pa-al) “she shall pay”, taken as a present (a G present would be ippal; the u- is unexplained), in šaniam ul uppal, UNCERTAIN
glossary.awīlum: man; the free citizen, the code’s first legal class
glossary.aššatum: wife: ana aššatišu “to his wife” · aššassu (SAL-zu, ZU for -ssu) “his wife” · construct aššat (aš-ša-at) “wife of” before a genitive: aššat awīlim · aššatam, aššatim, aššatum, written SAL (the same sign as zinništum “woman”) or aš-ša-tam · aššātim (aš-ša-tim) “wives”, the plural (aššātim iḫuz “he has taken wives”; the signs could also spell the singular aššatim) · aššat (SAL, bare, construct) in aššat Marduk ša Bābilim “a wife of Marduk of Babylon”, the title of a priestess of the god; her status UNCERTAIN
glossary.aḫum-brother: brother (aḫum): aḫḫū (aḫ-ḫu) “brothers” (nominative plural), aḫīšunu (a-ḫi-šu-nu) “their brother” (aḫum + -šunu “their”) · aḫḫūša (aḫ-ḫu-ša) “her brothers” (nominative plural + -ša), aḫḫīša (aḫ-ḫi-ša) “of her brothers” (genitive plural): ša aḫḫīšama “that of her brothers alone”, itti aḫḫīša “with her brothers”
glossary.balāṭum: to live; D-stem bulluṭum — muballiṭ “who gives life” · stative baltat (ba-al-ṭa-at) “she lives”, in adi baltat “as long as she lives”
glossary.baqārum: to claim, make a claim against (Harper: BAKARU “to make claim”): ibaqqarūši (i-ba-qa₂-ru-ši, present plural, “they shall claim against her”) with -ši “her”; Harper prints the sign as ga, read qa₂ · ibaqqarūši also written i-ba-aq-qa₂-ru-ši (AK read aq + GA read qa₂): aḫḫūša ul ibaqqarūši “her brothers shall not make any claim against her”
glossary.bītum: house, estate · bīt karānim “wine-house, tavern” (construct form bīt, written É); bītiša “her house” (É-ša) · bīt awīlim “a man’s house”; bīssa (bi-za, É-za) “her house”, written with É or syllabically with BI + ZA; bītišu (É-šu) “his house”; genitive bītim, accusative bītam, written É alone
glossary.eli: against, upon · with suffixes: elišu, eliša, elišunu “upon him, her, them” (of a debt)
glossary.emūqum: strength, power; the means of a house: emūq (e-mu-uq, no ending written, construct state “strength of”) in kīma emūq zittiša “in proportion to the strength of her share” and kīma emūq bīt abim “in proportion to the means of her father’s house” · noun
glossary.eqlum: field (written A.ŠÀ): eqelšu “his field” — the fief-land this whole block protects · bound form eqel (eqel itêšu “his neighbour’s field”; eqel ušākilu “the field he grazed”) · eqlam (A.ŠÀ, accusative) “the field”, eqlša (A.ŠÀ-ša) “her field”: eqlša u kirâša “her field and her orchard”
glossary.ilkum: the fief-duty — service owed to the crown for land held: ilikšu illak “he shall perform his duty”; the keyword of §§26–41 · ilkam (il-kam, accusative) in ilkam ul illak “she shall not perform the fief-duty”
glossary.ilum: god; here: the temple as owner · plural ilāni “gods” (written DINGIR.DINGIR, as in the litany): maḫar ilāni “before the gods”
glossary.ina: in, from · at (ina ebūrim “at harvest”); out of (ina bilat kirîm “out of the orchard’s yield”) · “through, by (means of)”: ina maḫāṣim “through beating”, ina pilšim “by a breach”; “regarding”: ina mimma ša … “regarding whatever …”; ina šanat “in the year”
glossary.irrišum: tenant, cultivator: irrišum, ana irrišim “to a tenant”; irrissu “his tenant” (irriš + -šu; Harper reads the same spelling as a verb, “he shall cultivate it”) · irrissa (ir-ri-za) “her tenant” (irriš + -ša, the š+š spelled with ZA): irrissa ittanaššiši “her tenant shall keep supporting her”
glossary.itti: with · “from”, after leqûm “to take”: itti šarrāqānišu ileqqi “from his thief he shall take”
glossary.izuzzum: to stand; izzazzu “he stands (in service)” · izzaz, izzazma (i-za-az, i-za-az-ma) “she shall stand (take her place)”, of an heir’s share: zittam kīma aplim ištēn izzazma “she shall take a share like one heir, and”; ul izzaz “she shall have no share”; sense UNCERTAIN
glossary.ištēn: one: šattam ištiatma “one year only” · ištiššu (iš-ti-iš-šu) “for the first time” (ištēn + -šu)
glossary.kallatum: bride (for a son), written with the Sumerogram É.GI₄.A, three signs and no ending written (Harper’s transliteration adds the ending, kal-lâtam): kallātam “a bride” · kallātim ({šal}É.GI₄.A) in §180: apparently a class of woman dedicated to a god, not “bride”; UNCERTAIN, the class cannot be defined
glossary.kaspum: silver — the code’s money, written KÙ.BABBAR “shining precious-metal” · kaspim: mišil mana kaspim “half a mina of silver” · with a spelled vowel after the logogram: KÙ.BABBAR-a-am, -i-im, -u-um: kaspam, kaspim, kaspum (accusative, genitive, nominative); kaspum as the subject; the grain-and-silver pair šeʾam u kaspam “grain and silver” · kasap (KÙ.BABBAR, no ending written) construct “silver of”: kasap tirḫatim “silver of the bride-price”
glossary.kirûm: orchard, garden (written {giš}SAR, the KIRI₆ sign): kirāšu “his orchard” · kirâm (accusative), kirâša (written {giš}KIRI₆, the -ša written out) “her orchard”: eqlam kirâm “the field, the orchard”
glossary.kunukkum: seal; sealed document · kunukkam (ku-nu-kam, ku-nu-uk-kam, the UG sign read uk) “a sealed tablet”, accusative: kunukkam išṭuršim “he has written her a sealed tablet”
glossary.kīma: like, as · as, like; with a verb in the subjunctive: kīma ubbalu “as he brings (it)” · according to: kīma ṣimdat šarrim “according to the king’s schedule” · “since, when”, before a stative: kīma mimmûšu lā ḫalqu “since his goods are not lost” · “in proportion to”: kīma emūq zittiša “in proportion to the strength of her share”, kīma emūq bīt abim “in proportion to the means of her father’s house”
glossary.leqûm: to take: ileqqi “he shall take” · ilqi “he took” (il-qi₂), ilqû (subjunctive, il-qu₂-u₂), ilqēma (il-qi₂-e-ma) “he took, and”, ilteqēma (perfect, il-te-qi₂-ma) “he has taken, and”; ša … ilqû “which he took” · ilqēma (il-qi₂-ma) “he took, and” (preterite ilqe + -ma, here without a spelled e); ilteqe (il-te-qi₂, perfect) “he has taken”; ileqqi (i-li-qi₂, present) “he shall take”; leqîm (li-qi₂-im, infinitive, genitive): ina kaspim leqîm “in the taking of the silver” · ileqqûma (i-li-qu₂-ma) “they shall take, and” (present plural + -ma); ileqqēma “he shall take, and” · ileqqû (i-li-qu₂-u) “they shall take” (present plural, without -ma)
glossary.libbum: heart · ana libbi “into”: ana libbi zittišu “into his share” · libbaša, libbiša (li-ib-ba-ša, li-ib-bi-ša) “her heart”: mala libbiša “as much as her heart wants”; libbaša uṭabbū “they shall make her heart good”, i.e. content her
glossary.lā: not (in subordinate and nominal contexts) · before a noun in the genitive, “without”: lā kanīkim “without a sealed receipt”; in a šumma-clause, “not”: lā ītamar “he did not see”
glossary.lū: or; either (lū … lū “whether … or”); with verb: “let …”
glossary.makkūrum: property, assets — written with the Sumerogram Harper reads ŠA.GA (modern NÍG.GA)
glossary.mala: as many as, as much as (introducing a relative clause): mala ina kirîm ibbaššû “as many as are in the orchard”
glossary.mazûm-Š: UNCERTAIN verb, the root not settled; read from the context as “to let (her) have her fill, as much as she wishes”: ušamziši (u-ša-am-zi-ši) “he has (not) let her have”, Š-stem preterite + -ši “her”; uštamziši (uš-tam-zi-ši) “he has let her have”, Š-stem perfect + -ši · Š-stem verb
glossary.mutum: husband (short u; Harper “husband”; mūtum “death” is another word, spelled the same, so the sense rests on context): mutiša “her husband”, mussa “her husband” (written mu-za, -ša after the t), mut “husband of” (construct; mut libbiša “the husband of her heart”) · mutiša panîm / warkîm “her former / later husband”, with mutiša followed by an adjective in the genitive · mutim (mu-tim, genitive) “husband”: ana mutim iddišši “he gave her to a husband”
glossary.mārtum: daughter (written DUMU+ti): mārtišu “his daughter” · mārassu (DUMU.SAL-zu, three signs DUMU + SAL + ZU, ZU for -ssu) “his daughter” · mārtaka (DUMU.SAL-ka) “your daughter”, mārtī (DUMU.SAL-i) “my daughter”, mārtim (DUMU.SAL, no ending written) “of the daughter”: abī mārtim “the father of the daughter” · mārtišu also written DUMU.SAL-šu (DUMU + SAL + ŠU) “his daughter”: ana mārtišu “to his daughter”
glossary.nadānum: to give, pay: inaddin, iddinam, iddinušum; nadānim “to give” · iddin “he gave”; ana kaspim nadānum “to sell”: inaddinūma (present, plural) “they shall sell, and …” · iddin, iddinu “he gave” (preterite; the subjunctive -u in a ša- or inūma clause); iddinma “he gave, and”; …in, …din in broken forms; inaddin “he shall give”: ana damqaršu inaddin “he shall give to his merchant” · ittadinma (it-ta-di-in-ma) “he has given, and” (perfect); inaddinu (i-na-ad-di-nu) “(which) he gives” (present, with the subjunctive -u) · ittandin (it-ta-an-di-in, perfect with an extra -n-) “he has handed over”: ana kiššātim ittandin “he handed over into service”; ittadin (it-ta-din) “he has given”, i.e. sold; ana maṣṣarūtim inaddin “he gives for safekeeping”; iddinūšumma “they gave him, and” · inaddin also of a woman, “she shall give” · inaddišši (i-na-ad-di-iš-ši) “he/she shall give her” (the n of the stem swallowed before -ši), of a sale: ana kaspim inaddišši “she may sell her”, ul inaddišši “she shall not sell her” · anaddin “I shall give”, with the n merged into the k of -kum: anaddikkum (a-na-ad-di-ik-kum) “I shall give (her) to you”; iddinu (id-di-nu) “(which) he gave”; iddinušum “he gave him” · nadānam (na-da-nam, infinitive accusative) “to give”: warkassa … nadānam “(that she may) give her estate” · iddišši (id-di-iš-ši) “he gave her”, preterite + -ši, the n written š: ana mutim iddišši “he gave her to a husband” · inaddinūši (i-na-ad-di-nu-ši) “they shall give her”, inaddinūšimma (i-na-ad-di-nu-šim-ma) “they shall give her, and”, ittadnūšimma (it-ta-ad-nu-ši-im-ma) “they have given her, and” (perfect plural + -šim + -ma) · iddinušim (id-di-nu-ši-im) “he gave her”, with the subjunctive -u in a ša-clause
glossary.našûm: to bear, carry: ittanašši “he shall bear (the penalty)” · našû (na-šu-u, stative with the subjunctive -u) “(that) he carried”: mimma ša našû “anything that he carried” · ittanaššiši (it-ta-na-aš-ši-ši, Gtn present + -ši) “he shall keep carrying (supporting) her” · iššīma (iš-ši-ma) “he has lifted (her), and”: ana ilim iššīma “he has dedicated (her) to a god”, literally “lifted up to a god”; the sense “dedicated” is UNCERTAIN
glossary.qadištum: a consecrated woman (qadištum is “the holy one”, from qadāšum “to be holy”), a class of woman, written {šal}NU.GIG (SAL + NU + GIG; Harper qadištu): qadištam “a qadištum” (accusative); her exact status is not settled, UNCERTAIN · noun
glossary.ugbabtum: UNCERTAIN: a priestess, written ŠAL.NIN.AN (Harper aššatum NIN.AN; NIN.AN is later written NIN.DINGIR, “lady of the god”); Harper gives no reading and translates only “a priestess”, later editions read ugbabtum, and the ŠAL may be only the woman-sign. The reading rests on the sign group and the context, not on a spelled word · here (§127) NIN.AN alone, with no ŠAL before it: ugbabtim “of a priestess”, still read ugbabtum, UNCERTAIN as before (Harper gives no reading) · in §178–179 NIN.AN is read ugbabtum as before, still UNCERTAIN; the separate SAL that follows it (Harper’s ŠAL(?)) is not part of the title here and is left unread (see SAL-sign)
glossary.warka: afterwards, later · as a conjunction before a clause, “after”: warka abum ana šīmtim ittalku “after the father has gone to his fate”
glossary.warkatum: the circumstances, the facts of the case: warkassu “his case” (warkat + šu, t+š → ss) · UNCERTAIN: warkassa (wa-ar-ka-za) “her case” (what is examined and decided) and “her estate” (what she leaves behind), the second reading resting on the context · the estate, the property left behind: warkat (wa-ar-ka-at, construct) bīt mutiša “the estate of her husband’s house”; warkassa (wa-ar-ka-za) “her estate” in the clause adi balṭat ikkal … warkassa ša mārīšama “her estate is her sons’ alone” (UNCERTAIN where the clause fits both senses)
glossary.zikrum-class: zikrum (zi-ik-ru-um) — the name of a class of woman, named beside the ugbabtum (NIN.AN) in §178–179 and beside the kallātim in §180; it is not zikrum “name” of the prologue, and what the class was is not known, UNCERTAIN · noun
glossary.zinništum: woman (written with the single sign SAL, ŠAL in Harper): zinništam, zinništim, zinništum
glossary.zittum: share, portion (written ḪA.LA): zittašu, zittišu “his share” · zittam (ṣi-it-tam, the ZI sign read ṣi by Harper and zi here, as in ezēbim) “a share”: zittam kīma aplim ištēn “a share like one heir’s”
glossary.Ì.BA: Ì.BA (Ì + BA; Harper writes NI.BA) — “oil ration” (Ì oil, BA allowance), one of the three rations of §178–179; the Akkadian word behind it is not read, UNCERTAIN · Sumerogram, Akkadian word not read
glossary.ēma: wherever; with the sense “to whomever”, before a clause with its verb in the subjunctive: ēma (e-ma) in warkassa ēma eliša ṭābu nadānam “her estate, wherever (to whomever) it pleases her, to give” · adverb / conjunction
glossary.ŠE.BA: ŠE.BA (ŠE + BA) — “grain ration” (ŠE grain, BA allowance), one of the three rations of §178–179; the Akkadian word behind it is not read, UNCERTAIN · Sumerogram, Akkadian word not read
glossary.šalšum: a third, one third (written IGI.3.GAL, three signs: IGI, the numeral 3, GAL): before a following noun šalšat “one third of”, a reconstructed construct form, marked (?) in the gloss: šalšat ablūtiša “a third of her heirship” · numeral / fraction, Sumerogram
glossary.šanûm: another, a second one: ana šanîm “to another”, šanûm “another man” · feminine šanītum “another (woman)”: šanītam, šanītim (ša-ni-tam, ša-ni-tim), in the accusative and genitive · šaniam (ša-ni-a-am, accusative) “another”: šaniam ul uppal “nor shall she pay another (?)”, UNCERTAIN
glossary.šarāqum-give: to give as a gift, to bestow (a dowry); kept apart from šarāqum “to steal”: išruq (preterite “he gave”) with -šim “to her”: išruqšim (iš-ru-uq-ši-im; iš-[ru]-uq-ši-im with the RU left out by the scribe; iš-ru-uq-šim with the single sign ŠIM), šeriqtam lā išruqšim “he has not given her a dowry”; with the subjunctive -u in a ša-clause, išruqušim (iš-ru-qu₂-ši-im) “(whom) he gave her”; išarraqūšima (i-šar-ra-qu₂-ši-ma) “they shall give her, and”, present plural + -ši + -ma · verb, G-stem
glossary.šaṭārum: to write; to assign in writing, deed over (Harper: išaddar): ul išaddar “he shall not deed” · išṭuršum (iš-tur-šum) “he wrote for him”: kunukkam išṭuršum “he wrote him a sealed document” · išṭurušim (iš-tu-ru-ši-im, with the subjunctive -u in a ša-clause), išṭuršim (iš-tur-ši-im), išṭuršimma (iš-tur-ši-im-ma) “he wrote for her (and)”, preterite + -šim: ina ṭuppim ša išṭurušim “in the tablet which he wrote for her”, lā išṭuršimma “he has not written for her, and”
glossary.šeriqtum: dowry, what the bride brings from her father’s house (§138 ša ištu bīt abiša ublam “which she brought from her father’s house”): šeriqtam “the dowry”, šeriqtaša “her dowry”. Harper reads it with q (še-ri-iq-ta-ša, the sign IG read iq) and later editions with k; UNCERTAIN in the form, the meaning rests on §138 · šeriqtiša (še-ri-iq-ti-ša) “her dowry”, šeriqti (še-ri-iq-ti, construct) “the dowry of”: šeriqtaša ša mārīšama “her dowry is her children’s alone”; šeriqtaša ša bīt abiša-ma “her dowry is her father’s house’s alone”
glossary.šugītum: UNCERTAIN: a class of woman named in §137, written {šal}šu-gi₄-tim (Harper prints šu-ge-tim): šugītim “(to) a šugītum”; the law sets her beside an ordinary wife as a woman who may bear children; her exact status is not known
glossary.šumma: if — the word that opens every law of the code
glossary.šīmtum: fate; one’s natural death: ana šīmtim ittalak “he went to (his) fate” = he died · plural šīmātum “fates”: šīmātīša (ši-ma-ti-ša) “her fates”; ina šīmātīša imtūt “she died in her fates” = she died a natural death
glossary.ṭuppum: the clay tablet; the deed: ṭuppašu iḫḫeppi “his tablet shall be smashed” — the sale annulled physically · ṭuppam (dup-pa-am, accusative), ṭuppim (dup-pi₂-im, genitive) “the tablet”: the tablet a father writes for his daughter, in which her dowry and her right to dispose of her estate are set down; kunukkam is the sealed one
glossary.ṭâbum: to be good, pleasing; D-stem ṭubbum “make good”; muṭīb “gladdener” · ṭābu (ṭa-bu, stative with the subjunctive -u) “(that) is pleasing”: eliša ṭābu “it is pleasing to her”
glossary.ṭâbum-D: to make good, to content, satisfy (literally “make the heart good”): libbaša uṭabbū (u-ṭa-ab-bu) “they shall content her”, D-stem present plural; uṭṭibbū (uṭ-ṭi-ib-bu) “they have contented (her)”, D-stem perfect, the form UNCERTAIN because of the doubled b · verb, D-stem
